title: Assisi embroidery
summary: Assisi embroidery is a voided cross-stitch from the Umbrian hill town of Assisi. The birds, beasts and flowers are left as bare linen and outlined in a dark double-running stitch, while the ground around them is filled with tiny cross-stitches, usually in a single colour.
howToPlay: Pick an outline thread from the cards and a motif from the tray.
Touch a square on the linen: the crosses step back, the shape is outlined in your thread, and its mirror partners follow.
Copy the chart shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The chart is mirrored left to right and top to bottom, so every shape you work is also worked on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its outline colour both match the chart you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: This counted work belongs to Assisi in Umbria, in central Italy, where medieval textile motifs of birds, animals and plants are stitched as bare shapes against a filled ground. It was revived as a local craft in the early twentieth century and is still taught and sold in the town.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original, in the style of the tradition)
